nodes.label: The Sierra Club Foundation

nodes.label: Laird Norton Family Foundation

nodes.label: Daughters of Charity, Province of St. Louise

nodes.label: Sisters of the Sorrowful Mother

nodes.label: Society of Jesus, USA Northeast Province (Jesuits USA East)

nodes.label: The Church Pension Fund (Episcopal)

nodes.label: Evangelical Lutheran Church in America (Corporate Social Responsibility program)

nodes.label: Reform Pension Board

nodes.label: The Pension Boards United Church of Christ

nodes.label: Unitarian Universalist Association

nodes.label: Christian Church Foundation (Disciples of Christ)
nodes.description: Votes proxies and engages companies as a responsible shareholder through its ICCR membership.

nodes.label: Union Theological Seminary

nodes.label: Church of God in Christ (COGIC)
nodes.description: ICCR faith-based member with a seat on the ICCR board, held by the director of its First Jurisdiction of Eastern New York urban initiatives and social justice ministry.

nodes.label: Bon Secours Mercy Health
nodes.description: Catholic health system that co-files shareholder proposals, including the 2025 Ford proposal on DEI policy changes and the 2026 Target proposal on pesticides.

nodes.label: Catholic Health Association of the United States
nodes.description: ICCR member that filed a November 2026 SEC comment opposing rescission of Rule 14a-8, defending the shareholder resolution process its member health systems use to engage companies.

nodes.label: Trinity Health
nodes.description: Catholic health system that files shareholder proposals and exempt solicitations, including smokefree casino reports at Wynn Resorts (2025) and Bally's (2024) and a 2023 Pfizer proposal on patent exclusivities and access.

nodes.label: Shareholder Rights Group

nodes.label: Center for Political Accountability

nodes.label: AIDS Healthcare Foundation

nodes.label: American Nonsmokers' Rights Foundation
nodes.description: Files shareholder resolutions with partners at casino operators (Boyd, Caesars, Wynn, Penn) asking for reports on the financial effects of smokefree indoor policies.

nodes.label: Heartland Initiative

nodes.label: Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center (formerly Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights), Compass Investors

nodes.label: Investor Environmental Health Network (project of Clean Production Action)

nodes.label: People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA)

nodes.label: Green America

nodes.label: US SIF: The Forum for Sustainable and Responsible Investment
nodes.description: Membership association that defends the shareholder proposal process, keeps a proxy proposal archive, and co-signed the 2026 petition on Rule 14a-8.

nodes.label: Shareholder Advocacy Forum (project of Americans for Tax Reform)

nodes.label: Amazon Watch

nodes.label: Rainforest Action Network
nodes.description: Campaigns on bank proxy votes, for example urging Bank of America shareholders in 2024 to back lobbying and energy financing ratio proposals and a Majority Action board campaign.

nodes.label: Athena

nodes.label: Color of Change
nodes.description: Campaigns on tech company shareholder votes, signing the 2022 civil society letter urging Alphabet's founders to back a racial equity audit proposal.

nodes.label: Union of Concerned Scientists
nodes.description: Science nonprofit that describes itself as an institutional investor and supplies scientific advice and analysis to networks of sustainable and responsible investors; it opposed the 2019 SEC limits on shareholder proposals.

nodes.label: New York Foundation

nodes.label: The California Wellness Foundation
nodes.description: Co-filed a 2026 shareholder proposal with the New York Foundation at Home Depot on oversight of customer data from third-party license plate reader surveillance cameras.

nodes.label: Park Foundation

nodes.label: Jessie Smith Noyes Foundation
nodes.description: Uses screening, proxy voting and shareholder engagement, introducing or supporting resolutions on social justice and environmental sustainability; ICCR member.

nodes.label: The Heritage Foundation

nodes.label: Council of Institutional Investors (CII)

nodes.label: International Corporate Governance Network (ICGN)

nodes.label: The Investor Forum

nodes.label: ChemSec Investor Initiative on Hazardous Chemicals (IIHC)

nodes.label: Access to Medicine Foundation

nodes.label: Platform Living Wage Financials (PLWF)

nodes.label: VBDO (Dutch Association of Investors for Sustainable Development)

nodes.label: Shareholders for Change (SfC)

nodes.label: Phoenix Group

nodes.label: Ninety One

nodes.label: Generali Investments

nodes.label: QIC

nodes.label: Rest

nodes.label: British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (BCI)

nodes.label: Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP)

nodes.label: Mackenzie Investments

nodes.label: Royal London Asset Management

nodes.label: Rathbones Group

nodes.label: Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS)

nodes.label: Local Authority Pension Fund Forum (LAPFF)

nodes.label: Sampension

nodes.label: PKA

nodes.label: Alecta

nodes.label: Ohman Fonder
nodes.description: Swedish fund manager that co-filed the 2024 workers' rights proposal at Amazon.

nodes.label: AP7 (Seventh Swedish National Pension Fund)
nodes.description: Swedish state default pension fund that takes part in the Big Tech and Human Rights investor collaboration.

nodes.label: Cardano Group
nodes.description: Pension investment and advisory group that co-filed the 2024 SHARE-led workers' rights proposal at Amazon.

nodes.label: PGGM
nodes.description: Dutch pension investment manager that co-filed a 2024 worker-driven social responsibility proposal at Nike and takes part in the Big Tech and Human Rights investor collaboration.

nodes.label: APG Asset Management
nodes.description: Dutch pension investment manager that takes part in the Big Tech and Human Rights investor collaboration.

nodes.label: Achmea Investment Management
nodes.description: Dutch manager whose engagement program covers climate, biodiversity, human rights and health, and whose Q4 2025 voting report names responsible AI use as a focus area.

nodes.label: Mirova
nodes.description: French sustainable investment manager (Natixis IM affiliate) that publishes annual engagement priorities and reports on climate, biodiversity and social issues.

nodes.label: Sycomore Asset Management
nodes.description: French SRI manager that co-filed the 2024 Ethos-led resolution asking TotalEnergies to separate the Chair and CEO roles.

nodes.label: Meeschaert Amilton Asset Management
nodes.description: French SRI manager that coordinated a group of eleven European investors filing a 2020 climate resolution at Total.

nodes.label: Etica Sgr
nodes.description: Italian responsible investment manager that runs a campaign on responsible AI, signed the Investor Statement on Ethical AI and joins the WBA Collective Impact Coalition for Ethical AI.

nodes.label: Union Investment
nodes.description: German asset manager that votes at company AGMs under its own proxy voting policy and keeps a separate engagement policy.

nodes.label: DNB Asset Management
nodes.description: Norwegian manager that engages through voting, dialogue and screening and has engaged a large technology company on AI governance through the WBA Collective Impact Coalition.

nodes.label: Australasian Centre for Corporate Responsibility (ACCR)

nodes.label: Australian Council of Superannuation Investors (ACSI)
nodes.description: Member body of Australian asset owners that engages ASX-listed companies on ESG and governance and publishes an annual stewardship report.

nodes.label: Market Forces

nodes.label: Alphinity Investment Management

nodes.label: Australian Ethical
nodes.description: Ethical fund manager and super fund whose in-house impact and ethics team applies its Ethical Criteria to investments.

nodes.label: Cbus Super

nodes.label: HESTA

nodes.label: Guardians of New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super Fund)

nodes.label: Canadian Coalition for Good Governance (CCGG)
nodes.description: Coalition of Canadian institutional investors that runs a board engagement program with Canadian public companies on governance practices.

nodes.label: Desjardins Global Asset Management (DGAM)
nodes.description: Quebec asset manager whose responsible investment team uses dialogue and proxy voting as its main tools for influencing issuers.

nodes.label: Mouvement d'education et de defense des actionnaires (MEDAC)

nodes.label: Kiko Network

nodes.label: Asia Research and Engagement (ARE)

nodes.label: Asset Management One
nodes.description: Japanese asset manager whose 2025 sustainability report lists AI and digital innovation among its materiality themes, describes an engagement on AI data center energy demand, and names human rights as a focus area.

nodes.label: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management (SuMi TRUST AM)
nodes.description: Japanese asset manager whose 2024-2025 stewardship report covers its business and human rights engagement and ESG points to consider with fast-spreading AI.

nodes.label: Nomura Asset Management
nodes.description: Japanese asset manager whose 2025 responsible investment report includes sections on human rights and on cybersecurity and AI ethics in its engagement.

nodes.label: ShareAction
nodes.description: UK charity that runs investor initiatives and helps savers and investors co-file shareholder resolutions and question companies at AGMs.

nodes.label: Advance (PRI)

nodes.label: BSR Investor Working Group on Responsible AI

nodes.label: T. Rowe Price
nodes.description: Mutual fund family whose corporate governance team publishes reviews of each proxy season and votes under its own proxy voting guidelines.

nodes.label: PRI

nodes.label: Goldman Sachs Asset Management
nodes.description: Asset management arm of Goldman Sachs, whose Global Stewardship Team runs proxy voting and company engagement.

nodes.label: Franklin Templeton
nodes.description: Global asset manager whose specialist investment managers run their own stewardship, supported by a firmwide Stewardship and Sustainability Council.

nodes.label: Morgan Stanley Investment Management
nodes.description: Asset management division of Morgan Stanley, whose Global Stewardship Team coordinates proxy voting and investee engagement.

nodes.label: Invesco
nodes.description: Global asset manager whose investment stewardship team supports proxy voting and engagement across its investment teams.

nodes.label: M&G Investments
nodes.description: UK asset manager whose Corporate Finance and Stewardship team leads voting and engagement.

nodes.label: Neuberger Berman

nodes.label: Microsoft 2023: Report on AI Misinformation and Disinformation
nodes.topic: Harms to people using AI products
nodes.subtopic: Generative AI misinformation/disinformation risk report
nodes.support_note: Microsoft reports 21.16% "Votes For", which matches For/(For+Against) to within 0.01 (Microsoft appears to truncate rather than round).
nodes.plain_summary: Asks the board for an annual report on risks from Microsoft's role in AI-generated or AI-spread misinformation and disinformation, its planned remediation steps, and their effectiveness.

policy_coverage.note: The EU AI Act requires AI-generated content to be machine-marked and deepfakes labeled from August 2026; it requires no report on misinformation risks or remediation effectiveness.

Providers of EU systemic-risk models must assess and mitigate systemic risks and report serious incidents to the AI Office; the Act's recitals name disinformation as a possible systemic risk, but its articles require no public misinformation report.

The voluntary GPAI Code names harmful manipulation as a systemic risk and lists a tendency to produce misinformation, and false content, among risk sources to consider; it binds only signatories and requires no public misinformation report.
Voluntary: the G7 Code asks developers to use content authentication and provenance, such as watermarking, where feasible; it requires no misinformation risk report.
Large generative AI providers must offer a free detection tool and embed latent disclosures in AI images, video and audio from August 2, 2026; no misinformation risk report is required.

Very large platforms and search engines must assess and reduce systemic risks to civic discourse and elections and publish risk reports; this covers their services, not a report on generative AI misinformation as such.
The guidelines expect labels on AI-generated content and red-teaming of generative AI before elections, or equally effective measures; no public misinformation report is required.
Intermediaries in India that enable AI content must label it and embed metadata, and social media intermediaries must get and verify user declarations; no risk report is required.
Korea requires notice of generative AI use and labels on its outputs; it does not require reports on misinformation risks.
Deepfake providers in China must label synthetic content and not produce fake news; there is no duty to report on misinformation risks.
Generative AI providers must improve accuracy and reliability, label images and video and act on illegal content; no misinformation risk report is required.

AI services covered by China's algorithm, deep synthesis and generative AI rules must add metadata labels, plus visible labels where content may confuse the public and platforms must flag AI content; it addresses labeling, not assessment or reporting of misinformation risks.

nodes.label: Microsoft 2024: Report on AI Data Sourcing Accountability
nodes.topic: Harms to people using AI products
nodes.subtopic: Ethics and legality of external data used to train AI (privacy/copyright)
nodes.support_note: Microsoft reports 36.19% "Votes For", which matches For/(For+Against) to within 0.01 (Microsoft appears to truncate rather than round).
nodes.plain_summary: Asks for an annual report on risks from unethical or improper use of external data to train Microsoft's AI offerings, how it mitigates them, and how it measures effectiveness.

policy_coverage.note: The EU AI Act makes general-purpose model providers publish a training-content summary and keep a copyright policy; it does not require a report on data-misuse risks or how well mitigations work.
The voluntary GPAI Code's copyright chapter commits signatories to respect web crawling opt-outs and handle complaints; it does not cover user data or require a risk report.
Colorado SB 26-189 makes developers give deployers the categories of training data used, to the extent known, from 2027; nothing is published to investors.
Voluntary: the G7 Code asks developers to apply data quality controls and protect personal data and intellectual property; it requires no public data report.
Generative AI developers must post public training data documentation, including whether it holds personal information, from 2026; it does not require a report on data-misuse risks or user data.
Under the GDPR as read by the EDPB, training on personal data needs a lawful basis tested case by case and can taint later model use; there is no duty to report publicly on training data.
Meta must offer EU users an objection route and other safeguards before training on their public posts and report to the DPC; the report goes to the regulator, not investors.
Training data must come from lawful sources, respect IP and have consent for personal data, and providers must explain data sources to regulators on request; no public disclosure is required.
Deepfake providers must secure training data, follow personal data rules and get separate consent to edit faces or voices; no public reporting is required.
Generative AI providers must strengthen security management of training data; the rule is general and has no disclosure duty.
AI companion providers must use lawfully sourced training data, guard against data poisoning and assess synthetic data; this covers one service type only.

nodes.label: Microsoft 2025: Report on Risks of Censorship in Generative AI
nodes.topic: Harms to people using AI products
nodes.subtopic: GenAI bias against religious or political views (civil rights)
nodes.support_note: Microsoft reports 0.69% "Votes For", which matches For/(For+Against) to within 0.01 (Microsoft appears to truncate rather than round).
nodes.plain_summary: Asks the board for a report on how it oversees risks of generative AI bias against religious or political views and whether such bias affects people's civil rights.

policy_coverage.note: The EU AI Act requires bias checks on high-risk systems' training data, now delayed to December 2027; it does not cover chatbot viewpoint bias or require a public report.

Colorado SB 26-189 requires notices, explanations and human review for automated decisions in jobs, lending, housing and other consequential areas from 2027, and drops the 2024 act's duty of reasonable care against algorithmic discrimination; it does not cover viewpoint bias or require public reports to investors.
The voluntary GPAI Code lists non-discrimination among risks signatory model providers should consider; it requires no public bias report.
NYC employers using automated hiring tools must publish annual independent bias audit summaries; the duty falls on employers in one city, not on AI vendors.
Illinois employers may not use AI with discriminatory effects in employment decisions from 2026; it covers one state and requires no public bias report.
TRAIGA bars AI developed or deployed with intent to unlawfully discriminate, but disparate impact alone is not enough; no bias testing or reporting.
Federal LLM contracts must require ideological neutrality and truth-seeking, which touches viewpoint bias; it applies only to models sold to federal agencies and requires no public report.
Korean high-impact AI operators must run risk management, give explanations and keep human oversight; there is no public bias report duty.

Providers must take effective measures to prevent discrimination by ethnicity, belief, country, region, sex, age, occupation or health in design and training data; no public bias audit or report is required.
Automated decisions using personal data must be transparent and fair with no unreasonable price discrimination; there is no reporting duty.
Recommendation services may not use algorithms for unreasonable price discrimination against consumers; broader bias review or reporting is not required.

nodes.label: Microsoft 2026: Additional Disclosures Meeting Climate Commitments (AI data centers)
nodes.topic: Data center externalities
nodes.subtopic: Climate commitments under AI data center energy demand and embodied carbon (the supporting statement cites generative AI)
nodes.plain_summary: Asks Microsoft to disclose additional information each year, beyond current disclosures, showing how it will manage its climate commitments as its emissions grow.

policy_coverage.note: The EU AI Act makes general-purpose model providers document a model's known or estimated energy use for regulators on request; it requires no public data center emissions, energy or climate-goal reporting.
Voluntary: the 2023 Guidelines expect companies to set and report on emissions targets consistent with the Paris Agreement; they say nothing specific about data centers.
Texas makes loads of 75 MW or more pay interconnection study costs and disclose backup generation to the grid operator; it covers grid costs in ERCOT only, not emissions or investor reports.
Oregon puts users of 20 MW or more in their own rate class so data centers bear their grid costs; no emissions or public energy reporting.
Georgia Power may charge new customers above 100 MW their full transmission, distribution and generation costs; it is a utility rule in one state and requires no company disclosure.

EU data centers of 500 kW or more must report energy use, efficiency, renewable share and waste heat each year to an EU database; per-site data is not published and no company climate goals are required.
Companies in CSRD scope must report scope 1 to 3 emissions and energy use where material, which takes in data centers; it is not data center specific and Omnibus I narrowed who reports.
GB 40879 sets mandatory energy efficiency limits for new and expanded data centers in China; it does not require emissions or cost reporting.
The plan caps PUE for new large data centers in China at 1.25 (1.2 at hubs) through project energy review; it does not require company disclosure of energy, emissions or costs.
PUE, green electricity share and renewable energy plans become review criteria for new computing facilities in China; no public company reporting is required.

Voluntary: certification requires top management to set an AI policy, assign roles and run AI risk and impact assessments; nothing is published to investors.
Voluntary: signatories pledged to publish frontier safety frameworks and report on implementation; covers severe risks only, not board oversight.
EO 14110 made developers of large dual-use foundation models report red-team results to Commerce, not the public; revoked January 20, 2025.

Korea requires risk management, documentation and human oversight for high-impact AI and safety duties for large models; it does not require board oversight disclosures.

Providers must set up algorithm review and ethics review systems, publish basic principles of their recommendation algorithms and, for services with public-opinion capacity, file algorithm self-assessment reports with the CAC; filings go to the regulator, not to shareholders.
Generative AI services with public-opinion capacity need security assessments and algorithm filing; these go to regulators and do not require board oversight.
Companies doing AI research in ethically sensitive areas must set up ethics review committees; there is no board-level oversight or public reporting duty.

AI companion providers must submit security assessment reports to provincial regulators at launch, after major changes and on reaching 1 million registered or 100,000 monthly active users; nothing is published to investors.
