nodes.label: UN Human Rights Council endorses the Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
nodes.description: Voluntary standard: companies should carry out human rights due diligence on impacts they cause, contribute to or are linked to through business relationships, which for AI vendors includes customer use of their products, and report on how they address them.

nodes.label: China adopts the Personal Information Protection Law
nodes.description: In force from November 1, 2021, it requires any company that uses personal data for automated decisions in China to keep those decisions transparent and fair, bars unreasonable price discrimination, and requires a non-personalized option or easy opt-out for automated content pushes and marketing (Article 24). People can demand an explanation of, and refuse, decisions made solely by automated means that significantly affect them.

nodes.label: China issues Ethical Norms for New Generation AI
nodes.actor: National New Generation AI Governance Expert Committee (Ministry of Science and Technology)
nodes.description: Sets six basic ethical requirements (human welfare, fairness, privacy and security, controllability, accountability, ethics literacy) and 18 specific requirements for managing, developing, supplying and using AI. It is guidance for companies and institutions, with no penalties.

nodes.label: China sets a national energy efficiency limit standard for data centers (GB 40879-2021)
nodes.actor: State Administration for Market Regulation; Standardization Administration of China
nodes.description: Sets energy efficiency limit values and grades, measured by the ratio of total data center electricity to IT equipment electricity, for new, rebuilt and expanded data centers; edge data centers are excluded. Took effect 2022-11-01.

nodes.label: China publishes the Algorithmic Recommendation Provisions
nodes.actor: Cyberspace Administration of China; MIIT; Ministry of Public Security; SAMR
nodes.description: In force from March 1, 2022 for any company using recommendation algorithms in Chinese internet services: users must be able to switch off personalization or delete profile tags, minors must not be pushed harmful content or induced into addiction, scheduling algorithms must protect gig workers' pay and rest, and unfair algorithmic price discrimination is banned. Services with public-opinion or social-mobilization capacity must file their algorithms with the CAC within 10 working days and undergo security assessments.

nodes.label: CAC begins publishing the national algorithm filing registry
nodes.description: The CAC began publishing the names and filing numbers of algorithms filed under the Algorithmic Recommendation Provisions, searchable at beian.cac.gov.cn, and has kept adding batches through October 2026.

nodes.label: Ceres launches the Valuing Water Finance Initiative
nodes.description: 64 investors with $9.8 trillion launched an effort to engage 72 large corporate water users, including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple and Microsoft, on six Corporate Expectations for Valuing Water.

nodes.label: China publishes the Deep Synthesis Provisions
nodes.actor: Cyberspace Administration of China; MIIT; Ministry of Public Security
nodes.description: In force from January 10, 2023, providers of deepfake and other synthetic text, voice, image and video services must label generated content, keep logs, manage training data security, get separate consent before editing a person's face or voice, and not produce fake news. Providers with public-opinion capacity, and their technical supporters, must file under the algorithm registry.

nodes.label: Parnassus begins AI governance engagement with Intuit
nodes.description: Private engagement on AI policies, governance, staffing and resourcing. No filed proposal found. Start date is year only.

nodes.label: EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive enters into force
nodes.description: Large companies report under the European Sustainability Reporting Standards, including greenhouse gas emissions (scopes 1 to 3), energy, water and own-workforce and value-chain impacts where material, with first reports for financial year 2024 from the largest public-interest entities. EU subsidiaries of US tech groups are covered; non-EU parent reporting starts later.

nodes.label: Micron products fail China's cybersecurity review
nodes.actor: Cybersecurity Review Office (Cyberspace Administration of China)
nodes.description: The review office found Micron products sold in China posed serious network security risks to critical information infrastructure, so operators of that infrastructure must stop buying Micron products.

nodes.label: OECD updates Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises, adding technology due diligence
nodes.description: Voluntary guidelines now expect companies developing or selling technology to do risk-based due diligence on its use, including by customers, and set climate expectations such as emissions targets. Complaints go to government National Contact Points.

nodes.label: China puts gallium and germanium items under export control
nodes.actor: Ministry of Commerce; General Administration of Customs
nodes.description: From August 1, 2023, exporters need a dual-use export license to ship listed gallium and germanium items, materials used in chipmaking.

nodes.label: NYC begins enforcing Local Law 144 on automated hiring tools
nodes.actor: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
nodes.description: Employers and agencies using automated employment decision tools for NYC jobs must get an annual independent bias audit, publish a summary, and notify candidates.

nodes.label: China publishes the Interim Measures for Generative AI Services
nodes.actor: Cyberspace Administration of China; NDRC; Ministry of Education; MOST; MIIT; Ministry of Public Security; NRTA
nodes.description: In force from August 15, 2023 for anyone, Chinese or foreign, offering generative AI to the public in China, including through APIs: training data must come from lawful sources, respect IP and have consent for personal data; providers must prevent discrimination in design and training data, label generated images and video, guard against minors' over-reliance, and report illegal content. Services with public-opinion capacity need a security assessment and algorithm filing, and overseas services that break the rules can be blocked.

nodes.label: EU Digital Services Act duties apply to very large platforms
nodes.description: Designated very large platforms and search engines, including Meta's Facebook and Instagram, Google Search and YouTube, Amazon Store, Apple App Store, LinkedIn, Bing and X, must assess and reduce systemic risks each year, including risks to minors, civic discourse and elections, publish risk reports and independent audits, and offer a recommender option not based on profiling. On all online platforms, ads based on profiling with sensitive data, and profiling-based ads shown to minors, are banned (Articles 26 and 28).

nodes.label: China issues Trial Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Review
nodes.actor: Ministry of Science and Technology and nine other bodies
nodes.description: In force from December 1, 2023, companies and institutions doing AI research in ethically sensitive areas must set up ethics review committees, and research on algorithm models with public-opinion mobilization capacity or highly autonomous decision systems in risky settings needs additional expert review.

nodes.label: China announces the Global AI Governance Initiative
nodes.actor: Government of China (Cyberspace Administration of China publication)
nodes.description: A diplomatic statement of principles for AI governance, including a people-centered approach, respect for other countries' sovereignty when supplying AI, risk testing and opposition to using AI to interfere in other countries. It sets no company duties.

nodes.label: China publishes Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online
nodes.description: In force from January 1, 2024, platforms with very large numbers of minor users or major influence on minors must run regular minors' protection impact assessments, offer a minors' mode, set up an independent oversight body mostly of outside members, and publish a yearly minors' online protection social responsibility report. Fines for some breaches reach 50 million yuan.

nodes.label: First Valuing Water Finance Initiative benchmark
nodes.description: Ceres assessed the 72 focus companies against the Corporate Expectations; 94 investors with more than $17 trillion were then committed to engage them.

nodes.label: UK Online Safety Act becomes law
nodes.description: User-to-user and search services must assess and reduce risks of illegal content and, where children can use them, content harmful to children, under codes enforced by Ofcom with fines up to 18 million pounds or 10% of worldwide revenue.

nodes.label: G7 issues Hiroshima Process Code of Conduct for advanced AI developers
nodes.description: Voluntary code asking organizations that build advanced AI to manage risks across the lifecycle, publish transparency reports on capabilities and limits, disclose governance and risk policies, and use content authentication.

nodes.label: Biden signs EO 14110 on safe, secure and trustworthy AI
nodes.description: Used the Defense Production Act to make developers of large dual-use foundation models report training plans and red-team results to Commerce, and directed agency guidance on bias, privacy and watermarking.

nodes.label: Bletchley Declaration on frontier AI safety
nodes.description: 28 countries and the EU agreed that frontier AI developers have a strong responsibility for the safety of their systems, including through testing and evaluation. It is a nonbinding statement with no company duties.

nodes.label: UK launches the AI Safety Institute
nodes.description: A government body to test advanced AI models before and after release, with access agreed voluntarily with developers. It has no powers to compel companies.

nodes.label: ISO/IEC 42001 AI management system standard published
nodes.description: Voluntary, certifiable standard for an AI management system: top management sets an AI policy, roles, risk and impact assessments and controls. It requires no public reporting.

nodes.label: Microsoft AI misinformation proposal wins 21% support
nodes.actor: Arjuna Capital; Open MIC; Eko; Azzad
nodes.description: First-time proposal asked Microsoft to report on generative AI misinformation and disinformation risks. Microsoft opposed, citing a planned annual AI transparency report.

nodes.label: Apple shareholders reject AFL-CIO AI transparency proposal
nodes.description: Proposal sought a report on Apple's AI use and ethics. Apple said it already provides AI transparency. It received 37.5% of votes cast for and against, per Apple's 8-K.

nodes.label: EU requires data centers to report energy and water use
nodes.description: Delegated Regulation 2024/1364 under the Energy Efficiency Directive makes operators of EU data centers of 500 kW or more report energy use, power usage effectiveness, water use, renewable energy share and waste heat reuse to a European database each year, first by September 15, 2024. The Commission publishes aggregated figures, not per-site data.

nodes.label: UN General Assembly adopts first AI resolution on safe, secure and trustworthy AI
nodes.description: US-led resolution adopted without a vote encourages states and companies to develop AI that respects human rights. It is nonbinding and imposes no duties on companies.

nodes.label: Commission election guidelines for very large platforms cover generative AI
nodes.description: Guidelines under DSA Article 35 recommend that very large platforms and search engines label AI-generated content, red-team generative AI systems before release, and stop recommender systems spreading AI-made disinformation. Platforms that do not follow them must show the Commission equally effective measures. Formally adopted April 26, 2024.

nodes.label: CAC begins publishing the generative AI service filing registry
nodes.description: Lists generative AI services that completed filing under the 2023 Interim Measures and requires apps built on them to show the model name and filing number; by April 30, 2026, 868 services had been filed and 530 apps or features registered.

nodes.label: Microsoft publishes first Responsible AI Transparency Report
nodes.description: Inaugural annual report on how Microsoft builds, deploys and oversees generative AI, fulfilling a July 2023 White House commitment.

nodes.label: OECD updates its 2019 AI Principles
nodes.description: Revised Recommendation on AI addresses general-purpose and generative AI, adding safety, information integrity and environmental sustainability. It is addressed to governments and is not binding on companies.

nodes.label: Companies sign Frontier AI Safety Commitments at the Seoul AI Summit
nodes.actor: UK and Republic of Korea governments; signatory companies
nodes.description: Voluntary pledges by AI developers to publish safety frameworks setting risk thresholds and mitigations, and to report on how they meet them, with frameworks due before the next summit in France.

nodes.label: Majority of Meta independent holders back AI misinformation report
nodes.description: Filers say about 53.6% of non-insider votes supported the generative AI risk proposal; it failed overall due to dual-class shares.

nodes.label: Singapore publishes Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
nodes.description: Voluntary framework with nine dimensions, including accountability, data, trusted development, incident reporting, testing, security and content provenance. No legal duties.

nodes.label: Alphabet AI misinformation proposal gets 45.7% of independent votes
nodes.description: Generative AI risk report proposal failed but drew strong independent support, per filers.

nodes.label: Meta pauses EU AI training after Irish DPC request
nodes.description: After engagement with the DPC, Meta's lead EU privacy regulator, Meta paused plans to train its large language models on public Facebook and Instagram posts by adults in the EU and EEA.

nodes.label: UN General Assembly adopts China-led AI capacity-building resolution
nodes.description: Resolution on international cooperation on AI capacity-building, adopted by consensus with US support, asks for help for developing countries. Nonbinding; no company duties.

nodes.label: Open MIC refiles Microsoft AI risk proposal
nodes.description: Filers said the 2024 transparency report lacked detail and metrics on generative AI misinformation risks and asked for annual reporting.

nodes.label: China issues the Special Action Plan for Green and Low-Carbon Data Centers
nodes.actor: NDRC; MIIT; National Energy Administration; National Data Administration
nodes.description: Targets an average national data center PUE below 1.5 by end of 2025, requires new and expanded large and very large data centers to reach PUE of 1.25 or less and national hub projects 1.2 or less, sets stricter energy and water efficiency review for new projects, and aims for more than 80% green electricity at new hub data centers by end of 2025.

nodes.label: EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive enters into force
nodes.description: Large EU and non-EU companies must identify, prevent and remedy adverse human rights and environmental impacts in their own operations and chains of activities, and originally adopt a climate transition plan. Omnibus I later narrowed scope, removed the transition plan duty and moved application to July 2029.

nodes.label: EU AI Act enters into force
nodes.description: Risk-based AI regulation takes effect, with general-purpose AI provisions applying 12 months later and most high-risk rules later still.

nodes.label: Illinois amends Human Rights Act to cover AI in employment
nodes.description: From January 1, 2026, employers may not use AI that has a discriminatory effect in hiring, promotion or discharge decisions, or use ZIP codes as a proxy, and must notify employees when AI is used.

nodes.label: Council of Europe AI Framework Convention opens for signature
nodes.description: First binding international AI treaty (CETS 225). Parties must address AI risks to human rights, democracy and the rule of law, including by private actors, but may choose how. First signers included the US, UK, EU, Norway and Israel. Not yet in force.

nodes.label: Australia proposes mandatory guardrails for high-risk AI
nodes.actor: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
nodes.description: Proposals paper set out ten guardrails for high-risk AI, such as testing, transparency and human oversight, and options to make them mandatory. The government said in December 2025 it will not proceed with them at this time.

nodes.label: TC260 releases the AI Safety Governance Framework 1.0
nodes.description: A non-binding technical guide that classifies AI risks (model, data, system, and cyber, physical-world, cognitive and ethical application risks) and sets out technical and governance measures and safe development guidelines for developers and providers.

nodes.label: California enacts SB 942, the AI Transparency Act
nodes.description: Generative AI providers with over one million monthly users must offer a free AI detection tool and embed latent disclosures in AI images, video and audio, with an option for visible labels. AB 853 later moved the start to August 2, 2026.

nodes.label: China publishes the Network Data Security Management Regulations
nodes.description: In force from January 1, 2025, Article 19 requires data handlers that provide generative AI services to strengthen security management of training data and its processing and to prevent and handle data security risks.

nodes.label: FTC announces Operation AI Comply
nodes.description: Five enforcement actions, including against DoNotPay and Rytr, over deceptive AI claims or AI tools used to deceive. The FTC said there is no AI exemption from existing consumer protection law.

nodes.label: California enacts AB 2013 on generative AI training data transparency
nodes.description: From January 1, 2026, developers of generative AI offered to Californians must post documentation on their training data, including sources, whether it holds personal information or copyrighted material, and collection dates.

nodes.label: Ofcom says the Online Safety Act covers many generative AI chatbots
nodes.description: Open letter says AI-generated content shared on user-to-user services, user-built chatbots others can use, and AI tools that search several websites fall under Online Safety Act duties.

nodes.label: DeepSeek and 16 other Chinese firms sign the AI Safety Commitments
nodes.actor: Artificial Intelligence Industry Alliance (AIIA); China Academy of Information and Communications Technology
nodes.description: Voluntary industry commitments, closely modelled on the Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments, covering red-teaming, transparency about frontier model capabilities and limits, safety organization, risk research, data and infrastructure security and safety measures for open-source releases.

nodes.label: China bans dual-use exports to US military users and gallium, germanium and antimony exports to the US
nodes.description: Bans dual-use exports to US military users or uses and in principle denies licenses for gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the US, with stricter review for graphite. MOFCOM suspended the second clause from November 9, 2025 to November 27, 2026 (Announcement 2025 No. 72) and again from November 28, 2026 to January 27, 2027 (Announcement 2026 No. 59); the ban on military users stays in force.

nodes.label: China opens an antitrust investigation into Nvidia
nodes.description: SAMR opened a case into suspected violations of the Anti-Monopoly Law and of the conditions it set in 2020 when approving Nvidia's acquisition of Mellanox.

nodes.label: Brazil's Senate passes AI bill PL 2338/2023
nodes.description: Risk-based AI bill with duties for high-risk systems, generative AI and copyright remuneration; it has been in a Chamber of Deputies special committee since 2025 without a vote.

nodes.label: EDPB opinion on personal data in AI models
nodes.description: Opinion 28/2024, requested by the Irish DPC, says AI models trained on personal data are not always anonymous, that legitimate interest can be a legal basis only after a three-step test case by case, and that unlawful training can affect use of the model. Regulators apply it when enforcing the GDPR against model developers.

nodes.label: Italian Garante fines OpenAI 15 million euros over ChatGPT training data
nodes.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
nodes.description: The Garante found OpenAI trained ChatGPT on personal data without an adequate legal basis and breached transparency duties, fined it 15 million euros and ordered a six-month public information campaign. A Rome court annulled the decision in March 2026.

nodes.label: South Korea passes AI Basic Act
nodes.description: Comprehensive AI law (Law No. 20676, promulgated January 21, 2025) with duties for high-impact and generative AI providers and a domestic representative rule for large foreign companies, effective after a one-year transition.

nodes.label: Canada's AIDA dies when Parliament is prorogued
nodes.description: Bill C-27, which held the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act and a privacy law rewrite, died on the order paper; Canada has no federal AI statute.

nodes.label: BIS issues the AI Diffusion Rule
nodes.actor: Commerce Department, Bureau of Industry and Security
nodes.description: Interim final rule set worldwide license requirements and country tiers for advanced AI chips and controlled some frontier model weights, with compliance due May 15, 2025.

nodes.label: EO 14148 revokes EO 14110
nodes.description: Initial rescissions order revoked Biden's AI order on the first day of the new administration, ending its reporting directions for frontier developers.

nodes.label: EO 14179 orders removal of barriers to US AI leadership
nodes.description: Directed officials to review and undo actions taken under the revoked EO 14110, revise OMB AI memos, and produce an AI Action Plan within 180 days. No direct company duties.

nodes.label: Georgia regulators approve data center billing rule
nodes.description: Lets Georgia Power charge new customers above 100 MW for transmission, distribution and upstream generation costs, with minimum bills and contracts up to 15 years; the PSC reviews contracts.

nodes.label: First International AI Safety Report published
nodes.actor: Expert panel chaired by Yoshua Bengio
nodes.description: Scientific review of general-purpose AI capabilities and risks, commissioned at the 2023 Bletchley summit. It makes no recommendations and imposes no duties.

nodes.label: EU AI Act bans and AI literacy duty apply
nodes.description: Eight banned AI practices apply, including manipulative or exploitative AI, social scoring, untargeted scraping of facial images and emotion recognition at work or school, and providers and deployers must take measures for their staff's AI literacy. Commission guidelines on the bans followed on February 4, 2025; the 2026 omnibus recast the literacy duty as an obligation of means.

nodes.label: OECD launches the Hiroshima AI Process reporting framework
nodes.description: Voluntary framework for organizations to report publicly on how they apply the G7 Code of Conduct, covering risk assessment, transparency, governance, content provenance and data protection.

nodes.label: Paris AI Action Summit statement; US and UK do not sign
nodes.description: Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable AI for People and the Planet, signed by about 60 countries plus the EU and the African Union Commission, sets nonbinding priorities. The United States and United Kingdom did not sign. No company duties.

nodes.label: SEC staff issues SLB 14M, rescinding SLB 14L
nodes.description: Staff guidance restored the pre-2021 approach to the ordinary business and economic relevance exclusions, giving companies more room to exclude proposals, including on AI.

nodes.label: Commissioner Crenshaw criticizes SLB 14M
nodes.description: Dissenting statement said the bulletin changes the rules for excluding shareholder proposals mid-season.

nodes.label: UK AI Safety Institute renamed AI Security Institute
nodes.description: The renamed institute focuses on national security and crime risks from AI, adds a criminal misuse team with the Home Office, and the government said it will not focus on bias or freedom of speech. It imposes no company duties.

nodes.label: China publishes the Measures for Labeling AI-Generated and Synthetic Content
nodes.actor: Cyberspace Administration of China; MIIT; Ministry of Public Security; NRTA
nodes.description: In force from September 1, 2025 with a mandatory national standard: providers covered by the algorithm, deep synthesis and generative AI rules must add hidden labels in file metadata, and visible labels to text, audio, images, video and virtual scenes where content may confuse the public; platforms that distribute content must check for and display labels. Removing or forging labels is banned.

nodes.label: Virginia HB 2084 asks regulators to review large-customer rate classes
nodes.description: Directs the State Corporation Commission, in Dominion and Appalachian Power rate cases through mid-2027, to consider whether separate customer classes are reasonable; explicit data center language was removed before passage.

nodes.label: Delaware enacts SB 21 amending DGCL sections 144 and 220
nodes.description: Narrowed controlling-stockholder liability and books-and-records rights, responding to Chancery rulings like the Tesla pay case and to companies leaving Delaware.

nodes.label: China issues national standards on generative AI service security, training data and data annotation
nodes.actor: State Administration for Market Regulation; Standardization Administration of China (TC260)
nodes.description: Three recommended national standards (GB/T 45654, 45652 and 45674-2025) set security requirements for generative AI services, for pre-training and fine-tuning data, and for data annotation, with self-assessment methods for providers.

nodes.label: Companies reincorporate from Delaware to Nevada and Texas
nodes.actor: Tesla, SpaceX, Tripadvisor, Dropbox and others
nodes.description: Memo lists firms moving to Nevada and Texas after Chancery rulings. Later reports say the pace did not slow after SB 21 (this site has not confirmed the share figures).

nodes.label: Commission adopts AI Continent Action Plan
nodes.description: Plan for compute (including AI gigafactories), data, skills, adoption and simpler AI rules. It imposes no duties on companies itself; it led to the Cloud and AI Development Act proposal.

nodes.label: EU 'stop-the-clock' directive delays CSRD and CSDDD
nodes.description: Directive 2025/794 postponed CSRD reporting for companies not yet reporting by two years and pushed back CSDDD transposition and first application by one year, while the Omnibus content changes were negotiated.

nodes.label: US requires a license for Nvidia H20 chip sales to China
nodes.description: Nvidia disclosed it was told on April 9 that H20 exports to China need a license indefinitely and expected up to $5.5 billion in charges.

nodes.label: First Hiroshima AI Process reports published
nodes.description: OECD published the first round of voluntary reports from 19 organizations. From this site's company list: Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce and SoftBank Corp. (a SoftBank Group subsidiary). Amazon reported in Q4 2025 and Cohere in Q3 2026.

nodes.label: CAC launches the Qinglang campaign against AI technology misuse
nodes.description: A three-month enforcement campaign targeting unfiled AI services, face and voice cloning without consent, poorly managed training data, missing content labels, AI-made rumours and harm to minors.

nodes.label: BIS rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule and issues chip guidance
nodes.actor: Commerce Department, Bureau of Industry and Security
nodes.description: BIS said it would not enforce the diffusion rule and would replace it, and warned that using Huawei Ascend chips anywhere risks violating US export controls, with diligence expectations for chips used to train Chinese models.

nodes.label: Texas SB 29 codifies business judgment rule
nodes.description: Effective on signing; protects listed Texas companies' directors, lets companies set ownership thresholds for derivative suits, and aims to attract incorporations.

nodes.label: Texas SB 1057 raises shareholder proposal thresholds
nodes.description: Opt-in law lets companies require $1 million or 3% ownership, six-month holding, and solicitation of 67% of voting power. Effective September 1, 2025.

nodes.label: TAKE IT DOWN Act signed
nodes.description: Criminalizes publishing nonconsensual intimate images, including AI deepfakes, and requires covered platforms to remove reported images within 48 hours, with FTC enforcement from May 19, 2026.

nodes.label: Meta resumes EU AI training after Irish DPC review
nodes.description: After the EDPB opinion, Meta changed its plan and added safeguards, including an objection option, before training on adults' public Facebook and Instagram content from May 27, 2025. The DPC made recommendations and required Meta to report on how well the safeguards work in October 2025.

nodes.label: Japan enacts AI Promotion Act
nodes.description: Framework law (Act No. 53 of 2025) creating an AI Strategic Headquarters led by the Prime Minister and a Basic AI Plan. Businesses must make efforts to cooperate with government measures; there are no penalties or detailed compliance duties.

nodes.label: Oregon POWER Act (HB 3546) creates a rate class for large energy users
nodes.description: Directs the Public Utility Commission to put facilities using 20 MW or more, such as data centers, in a separate rate class so their grid costs are not shifted to households. Signing date per a law school summary.

nodes.label: UK Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 passed
nodes.description: Changes UK data protection law, including rules on automated decision-making, and requires the government (not companies) to publish an economic impact assessment and a report on copyright works in AI development, including developer disclosure of training data and web crawlers, within nine months.

nodes.label: Microsoft releases 2025 Responsible AI Transparency Report
nodes.description: Second annual report on Microsoft's responsible AI practices and customer support.

nodes.label: Texas SB 6 sets rules for large loads such as data centers
nodes.description: Loads of 75 MW or more in ERCOT pay interconnection study fees, disclose backup generation, and can be curtailed in grid emergencies. Effective on signing.

nodes.label: Texas enacts TRAIGA (HB 149)
nodes.description: From January 1, 2026, bars developing or deploying AI intended to incite self-harm, unlawfully discriminate, or produce child sexual abuse material or sexual deepfakes; disparate impact alone is not proof of intent. Attorney General enforces, with a cure period.

nodes.label: Intuit publishes AI governance and risk disclosure
nodes.description: Per Parnassus, Intuit released public AI governance and risk management disclosure in the first half of 2025. The date shown is approximate.

nodes.label: Senate votes 99-1 to strike state AI law moratorium
nodes.description: Proposed moratorium on state AI laws was removed from the budget reconciliation bill before passage.

nodes.label: EU publishes General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
nodes.description: Voluntary code with transparency, copyright, and safety and security chapters, offered as a way for model providers to show AI Act compliance.

nodes.label: OpenAI says it intends to sign EU AI code
nodes.description: OpenAI said it would sign the GPAI Code of Practice, subject to formal approval by the AI Board.

nodes.label: Commission publishes DSA guidelines on protecting minors
nodes.description: Guidelines under DSA Article 28 set out what online platforms minors can access should do on age assurance, grooming, harmful content, addictive design and commercial practices, including a risk review. They are not binding, but the Commission uses them as its benchmark when it checks compliance.

nodes.label: Meta refuses to sign EU AI code
nodes.description: Joel Kaplan said the code creates legal uncertainty and goes beyond the AI Act. Meta remained absent from the signatory list in 2026.

nodes.label: Anthropic announces it will sign EU AI code
nodes.description: After review, Anthropic said it intends to sign the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice.

nodes.label: White House releases America's AI Action Plan
nodes.description: Over 90 nonbinding federal actions on innovation, infrastructure and diplomacy, plus executive orders including faster permitting for data centers.

nodes.label: EO 14318 speeds federal permitting for data centers
nodes.description: Fast-tracks federal permits, environmental reviews and financing for data center projects needing over 100 MW of new load for AI. Eases rules for companies; adds no duties.

nodes.label: EO 14319 on 'Preventing Woke AI' in federal procurement
nodes.description: Agencies may buy only large language models that meet two Unbiased AI Principles, truth-seeking and ideological neutrality, with contract terms set through OMB guidance. Applies only to federal purchases.

nodes.label: EO 14320 promotes exports of the American AI technology stack
nodes.description: Creates a Commerce-led American AI Exports Program inviting industry consortia to propose full-stack AI export packages backed by federal financing tools. No duties.

nodes.label: Ofcom's children's safety codes take effect
nodes.description: Services in scope of the Online Safety Act that allow pornography or content promoting self-harm, suicide or eating disorders must use highly effective age checks, and services children use must have finished children's risk assessments and give age-appropriate experiences.

nodes.label: China releases the Global AI Governance Action Plan
nodes.actor: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China
nodes.description: A 13-point diplomatic plan released at the World AI Conference, including calls to jointly set AI energy and water efficiency standards, eliminate algorithmic bias, protect personal data and support UN-based AI governance. It sets no company duties.

nodes.label: Chinese industry releases the China AI Safety Commitments Framework
nodes.actor: China AI Safety and Development Association (CnAISDA); CAICT
nodes.description: An expanded voluntary commitment framework, built on the December 2024 AIIA commitments, adding international safety cooperation and frontier AI risk prevention; CAICT said it would promote disclosure and testing by signatory firms.

nodes.label: Google says it will sign EU AI code
nodes.description: Google committed to sign while voicing concerns that parts of the code and AI Act could slow innovation in Europe.

nodes.label: Microsoft confirms it will sign EU AI code
nodes.description: Microsoft publicly shared its decision to become a signatory a day after Google, per trade press.

nodes.label: CAC summons Nvidia over H20 chip security risks
nodes.description: Citing reported tracking and remote shutdown capabilities in Nvidia computing chips, the CAC required Nvidia to explain the backdoor and vulnerability risks of H20 chips sold in China and submit supporting evidence.

nodes.label: xAI signs only safety chapter of EU AI code
nodes.description: xAI joined the Safety and Security chapter only, calling the rest overreach, so it must show transparency and copyright compliance by other means.

nodes.label: EU AI Act obligations for general-purpose models apply
nodes.description: GPAI providers must meet transparency and copyright duties; models already on the market have until August 2, 2027.

nodes.label: OpenAI urges Newsom to harmonize California AI rules
nodes.description: Letter asked California to treat compliance with federal or EU frameworks, such as the EU code, as satisfying state AI safety rules.

nodes.label: UN creates Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and Global Dialogue on AI Governance
nodes.description: Resolution 79/325, adopted by consensus, sets up a 40-member scientific panel with an annual report and a Global Dialogue for governments and stakeholders. No company duties.

nodes.label: State Council issues Opinions on the AI Plus action
nodes.description: Sets national goals for AI adoption across science, industry, consumption, public welfare and governance, including more than 70% uptake of new smart devices and AI agents by 2027 and more than 90% by 2030. It is an industrial policy, not a set of company duties.

nodes.label: Colorado delays AI Act to June 30, 2026
nodes.description: Special-session bill SB 25B-004 moved the effective date from February 1, 2026. The 2026 session then repealed and replaced the act with SB 26-189 (see next event).

nodes.label: ExxonMobil launches first US retail standing voting program
nodes.description: After an SEC no-action letter in September 2025, Exxon let retail holders give standing voting instructions. The day shown is approximate.

nodes.label: Anthropic endorses California SB 53
nodes.description: Anthropic backed the frontier AI transparency bill, while major tech groups lobbied against it.

nodes.label: FTC opens 6(b) study of AI chatbots acting as companions
nodes.description: Compulsory orders to Alphabet, Character Technologies, Instagram, Meta, OpenAI, Snap and xAI ask how they test and monitor harms to children and teens, monetize engagement, and handle chat data. Answers go to the FTC, not the public.

nodes.label: EU Data Act starts to apply
nodes.description: Makers of connected products must let users access and share the data their devices generate, and cloud providers such as Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Oracle must let customers switch or use several providers, with switching and egress charges ending from January 12, 2027. Design duties for new connected products apply from September 2026.

nodes.label: China opens an anti-dumping investigation into US analog chips
nodes.description: Investigation, on a petition from the Jiangsu Semiconductor Industry Association, into interface and gate driver chips made at 40nm and above imported from the US.

nodes.label: China opens an anti-discrimination investigation into US chip measures
nodes.description: Investigates US tariffs, chip export controls since 2022, CHIPS Act limits and May 2025 guidance restricting use of Huawei Ascend chips and use of US AI chips to train Chinese models.

nodes.label: China finds Nvidia violated antitrust law and widens its probe
nodes.description: SAMR said a preliminary investigation found Nvidia violated the Anti-Monopoly Law and its 2020 Mellanox approval conditions, and it began a further investigation.

nodes.label: AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 released
nodes.description: Updates the 2024 framework with revised risk categories, risk grading and updated safety measures; it remains a non-binding technical document.

nodes.label: Ceres report 'Drained by Data' on data center water stress
nodes.description: Analysis with Cathay Financial Holdings and Bluerisk of data center water demand around Phoenix, covering cooling water and water used to generate their electricity, and the water-stress risk that can pose for companies.

nodes.label: Newsom signs SB 53, Transparency in Frontier AI Act
nodes.description: Large frontier developers must publish safety frameworks and transparency reports and report critical safety incidents; whistleblower protections; AG enforces penalties.

nodes.label: China extends rare earth export controls abroad, with case-by-case review for advanced chips and military AI
nodes.description: Requires foreign exporters of items containing Chinese rare earths to get Chinese licenses, with case-by-case review for uses in 14nm-and-below logic chips, 256-layer-and-above memory, related equipment and AI research with potential military use. Suspended from November 7, 2025 to November 10, 2026 (Announcement 2025 No. 70) and again from November 11, 2026 to January 10, 2027 (MOFCOM/GAC Announcement 2026 No. 58).

nodes.label: China opens an antitrust investigation into Qualcomm
nodes.description: SAMR opened a case because Qualcomm completed its acquisition of Autotalks without notifying the regulator.

nodes.label: California enacts SB 243 on companion chatbots
nodes.description: From January 1, 2026, companion chatbot operators must disclose the bot is AI, keep suicide and self-harm protocols, remind known minors to take breaks, and take reasonable steps to block sexual content for minors; private right of action.

nodes.label: California AB 853 delays and expands the AI Transparency Act
nodes.description: Moved SB 942's start to August 2, 2026 and added duties for large online platforms and generative AI hosting platforms from 2027 and capture-device makers from 2028.

nodes.label: China amends the Cybersecurity Law to add an AI article
nodes.description: In force from January 1, 2026, a new Article 20 commits the state to AI research, training data and computing infrastructure, AI ethics rules, and risk monitoring, assessment and safety supervision; the amendment also raises penalties for network operators.

nodes.label: Second VWFI benchmark, with a high-tech industry analysis
nodes.description: Assessed 71 focus companies; the high-tech analysis covers Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft and Sony and discusses data center and semiconductor water use. Tech industry average rose to 32.7 of 90 points from 23.7 in 2023.

nodes.label: India releases AI Governance Guidelines
nodes.description: Principle-based guidelines under the IndiaAI Mission that rely on existing laws and voluntary measures rather than a new AI law; no new binding company duties.

nodes.label: SEC staff stops responding to most 14a-8 no-action requests
nodes.description: For the season of October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026, staff said it would not respond to no-action requests except under Rule 14a-8(i)(1), citing post-shutdown resource limits. Companies still had to send Rule 14a-8(j) notices 80 days before filing a definitive proxy; a company that added an unqualified representation of a reasonable basis to exclude got a letter saying staff would not object, without staff evaluating it.

nodes.label: Commission proposes digital omnibus delaying AI Act rules
nodes.description: Proposal to push high-risk AI obligations back toward 2027 as part of a simplification package.

nodes.label: Australia's National AI Plan drops a standalone AI act
nodes.description: Plan relies on existing technology-neutral laws, with possible targeted changes, instead of mandatory AI guardrails or an AI act. No new company duties.

nodes.label: Australia's social media minimum age takes effect
nodes.description: Under the Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024, age-restricted platforms including Facebook, Instagram, Threads, X and YouTube must take reasonable steps to stop under-16s having accounts.

nodes.label: Executive order seeks national AI framework preempting state laws
nodes.description: EO 14365 creates a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, ties some state funding to AI laws, and asks for a preemptive federal framework.

nodes.label: Hochul signs New York RAISE Act for frontier AI
nodes.description: Requires large frontier developers to publish safety frameworks and report incidents within 72 hours; signed on condition of 2026 chapter amendments.

nodes.label: Japan adopts first AI Basic Plan
nodes.description: First plan under the AI Promotion Act aims for reliable AI and more staff at the Japan AI Safety Institute. No binding company duties.

nodes.label: Ofcom investigates X over Grok sexualized images
nodes.description: Formal investigation into whether X met its Online Safety Act duties to remove illegal content and protect children after Grok was used to make sexualized images. On February 3, 2026 Ofcom said it cannot currently investigate the standalone Grok service's creation of illegal images; by October 2026 Grok had restricted pornographic content for UK children after Ofcom engagement.

nodes.label: Microsoft launches Community-First AI Infrastructure commitments
nodes.description: Five commitments to datacenter communities, including not raising local electricity prices and protecting water supplies.

nodes.label: BIS moves H200-class chip exports to China to case-by-case review
nodes.actor: Commerce Department, Bureau of Industry and Security
nodes.description: Following a December 2025 presidential announcement, licenses for Nvidia H200, AMD MI325X and similar chips to China and Macau are reviewed case by case if exporters certify US supply, third-party testing and know-your-customer and remote-access safeguards.

nodes.label: South Korea's AI Basic Act and enforcement decree take effect
nodes.description: Providers must tell users in advance when a product uses high-impact or generative AI and label generative AI outputs; high-impact AI operators need risk management, explanation and human oversight; large foreign providers above revenue or user thresholds must name a Korean representative.

nodes.label: Commission opens DSA investigation into Grok on X
nodes.description: Formal proceedings examine whether X assessed and reduced the risks of rolling out Grok in the EU, including manipulated sexual images that may amount to child sexual abuse material, and widen the 2023 case on X's recommender systems. X must file an ad hoc risk assessment of Grok's functions.

nodes.label: Second International AI Safety Report published
nodes.actor: Expert panel chaired by Yoshua Bengio
nodes.description: Updated scientific review of general-purpose AI capabilities and risks, released ahead of the India summit; it reports that 12 companies published or updated frontier AI safety frameworks in 2025. No duties.

nodes.label: IIGCC publishes research on AI data center climate and nature risks
nodes.description: Insight covering data center emissions, water use for cooling and physical risk; IIGCC said it plans guidance, insights and engagement tools on data center operations, developed with members.

nodes.label: India requires labels on AI-generated content
nodes.description: Amended IT intermediary rules, in force February 20, 2026, define synthetically generated information: intermediaries that enable creating AI content must label it prominently and embed metadata; social media intermediaries must get users to declare AI content and verify it with technical measures.

nodes.label: India AI Impact Summit adopts New Delhi Declaration; US signs
nodes.description: About 88 countries and organizations, including the US, China, UK and EU, endorsed a nonbinding declaration (counts vary by source); frontier AI companies separately signed voluntary New Delhi Frontier AI Impact Commitments, including publishing aggregated data on AI's economic effects.

nodes.label: Omnibus I cuts back CSRD and CSDDD
nodes.description: The Omnibus I directive limits CSRD reporting to companies with over 1,000 employees and 450 million euros turnover, and limits the CSDDD to EU companies with over 5,000 employees and 1.5 billion euros turnover and non-EU companies with over 1.5 billion euros EU turnover. It deletes the CSDDD climate transition plan duty and sets CSDDD application for July 26, 2029. In force March 18, 2026.

nodes.label: Proponents sue companies that excluded proposals without SEC review
nodes.description: Law firm reports litigation against companies rose after the revised 14a-8 process; Skadden later counted six proponents suing six companies. Date is month of memo.

nodes.label: Australian online safety codes apply to AI companion chatbots
nodes.description: Industry codes registered in September 2025 require services, including generative AI services and AI companion chatbots able to produce sexually explicit, violent or self-harm material, to confirm users are 18 or over before giving access to it; some duties start later.

nodes.label: China adopts the 15th Five-Year Plan with AI governance goals
nodes.description: Calls for AI laws, ethics rules, algorithm filing, transparency and safety assessment systems, lifecycle AI risk management and measures to address AI's effects on employment.

nodes.label: Rome court annuls the Garante's OpenAI fine
nodes.description: The court held the Garante lacked competence because OpenAI's EU establishment in Ireland put the case under the GDPR one-stop-shop, led by the Irish DPC. It did not rule on whether the GDPR was breached.

nodes.label: UK government publishes report on copyright and AI
nodes.description: Report and impact assessment required by the Data (Use and Access) Act covering training data transparency, technical measures and licensing; commentators say it drops the earlier opt-out proposal. It imposes no duties on AI developers.

nodes.label: ICCR and As You Sow sue SEC over no-action pause
nodes.description: Suit in D.C. federal court argues the SEC changed how Rule 14a-8 works without notice-and-comment rulemaking under the APA. Pending as of latest reports.

nodes.label: New York amends RAISE Act to mirror California SB 53
nodes.description: Chapter amendment adopts SB 53's $500 million revenue threshold and cuts penalties to $1 million and $3 million. Effective January 1, 2027 (per law firm).

nodes.label: BlackRock Voting Choice covers about $851 billion
nodes.description: Index equity clients with about $851 billion in assets were using Voting Choice; eligible assets with individual investors reach about $3.96 trillion.

nodes.label: Court declines to order Chubb to include As You Sow's proposal
nodes.actor: U.S. District Court, District of Columbia
nodes.description: As You Sow v. Chubb Limited (26-734): the court denied a preliminary injunction over a climate-report proposal Chubb excluded on ordinary-business grounds, finding As You Sow "has not demonstrated that it is entitled to emergency injunctive relief". The opinion is a court-stamped filing hosted by Climate Policy Radar, not a court site.

nodes.label: China issues an action plan linking AI and energy
nodes.actor: NDRC; National Energy Administration; MIIT; National Data Administration
nodes.description: Makes renewable energy plans, PUE, green electricity share and waste heat recovery key criteria in energy and carbon review of new and expanded computing facilities, and promotes direct green power supply to them.

nodes.label: China publishes Interim Measures for anthropomorphic AI interaction services
nodes.actor: Cyberspace Administration of China; NDRC; MIIT; Ministry of Public Security; SAMR
nodes.description: In force from July 15, 2026 for AI companion and emotional interaction services: providers may not offer virtual partner or relative services to minors, need guardian consent for users under 14, must offer a minors' mode, intervene when users signal self-harm, avoid fostering dependence, and manage training data. Services with 1 million registered or 100,000 monthly active users must file security assessments with provincial regulators and complete algorithm filing.

nodes.label: Court orders BJ's Wholesale Club to include an excluded proposal
nodes.actor: U.S. District Court, District of Massachusetts
nodes.description: DiNapoli v. BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings (26-11075-LTS): the court granted the New York State Common Retirement Fund's motion for injunctive relief and denied BJ's motion to dismiss, rejecting its private-right-of-action, ordinary-business, Delaware-law and vagueness arguments. The order is a court-stamped filing hosted by a law firm, not a court site.

nodes.label: CAC penalizes Jianying, Maoxiang and Jimeng AI for missing AI labels
nodes.description: Local cyberspace offices summoned, warned and ordered corrections from the Jianying and Maoxiang apps and the Jimeng AI site for not properly labeling AI-generated content, under the labeling measures and generative AI rules.

nodes.label: Commission preliminarily finds Meta breaches DSA on under-13 users
nodes.description: Preliminary findings say Facebook and Instagram fail to identify, assess and reduce the risk of children under 13 using them, since a false birthdate is not checked.

nodes.label: UK Crime and Policing Act 2026 adds AI child abuse and chatbot powers
nodes.description: Section 72 will make it an offence, once commenced, to make, possess or supply tools designed to create child sexual abuse images (England and Wales). Section 248, in force, lets the Secretary of State extend Online Safety Act illegal content duties to any AI service by regulations; none have been made yet.

nodes.label: CAC launches the Qinglang campaign against AI application disorder
nodes.description: A four-month enforcement campaign against unfiled models, weak safety filtering, unlawful or unauthorized training data, data poisoning, missing labels, open-source model safety gaps and AI content that harms minors.

nodes.label: China issues Implementation Opinions on AI agents
nodes.actor: Cyberspace Administration of China; NDRC; MIIT
nodes.description: Sets principles for AI agents and tiered governance: in sensitive and key sectors, agents face filing, testing and recall of problem products, while low-risk uses rely on self-testing and reporting; it also targets addiction and emotional dependence risks for minors and older people.

nodes.label: State Council plans comprehensive AI legislation
nodes.actor: General Office of the State Council
nodes.description: The State Council's 2026 legislative plan calls for speeding up comprehensive legislation on the healthy development of AI. No draft AI law has been published.

nodes.label: Colorado repeals and replaces its AI Act with SB 26-189
nodes.description: SB 26-189 repeals and reenacts SB 24-205 as a law on automated decision-making technology used in consequential decisions (jobs, education, housing, lending, insurance, health care, government services). It drops the impact assessment duty, keeps consumer notices, explanations and human review, and takes effect January 1, 2027. The Attorney General enforces it; there is no private right of action.

nodes.label: EU ratifies the Council of Europe AI Convention
nodes.description: EU deposited the first instrument of ratification. The treaty needs five ratifications, three by Council of Europe members, to enter into force; this site found no other confirmed ratification.

nodes.label: FTC begins enforcing TAKE IT DOWN Act platform duties
nodes.description: Platform removal duties took effect May 19, 2026; the FTC sent warning letters to 12 operators of nudify tools, after reminder letters to 15 major platforms including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta and Microsoft.

nodes.label: Amazon data center energy proposal gets about 18% support
nodes.actor: As You Sow and co-filers; Amazon
nodes.description: Proposal on AI data center energy demand drew less support than a similar 2025 measure (20.1%). Date is report date.

nodes.label: Commission proposes Cloud and AI Development Act
nodes.description: Proposed regulation COM(2026) 502 aims to triple EU data center capacity in five to seven years with faster permits in acceleration zones and support for strategic data center projects; the data center rating scheme is meant to feed its sustainability assessments.

nodes.label: Great American AI Act discussion draft would preempt state AI model laws
nodes.actor: Reps. Jay Obernolte and Lori Trahan
nodes.description: A bipartisan House discussion draft, not yet introduced, would bar state laws specifically regulating AI model development for three years and add federal frontier-model duties similar to California SB 53 and New York's RAISE Act.

nodes.label: Canada tables Safe Social Media Act covering AI chatbots
nodes.description: Bill C-34 would bar children under 16 from social media, require operators of human-like chatbots to be transparent about their reporting thresholds in crisis situations and limit harmful content, and create a Digital Safety Commission.

nodes.label: Canada tables privacy bill with automated decision rules
nodes.description: Bill C-36, the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act, would modernize Canada's private-sector privacy law, add rules on automated decisions and children's data, and create a Digital Safety and Data Protection Commission. It does not revive AIDA.

nodes.label: China issues guidance on safe AI use in banking and insurance
nodes.description: 32 guidance points require banks and insurers using AI to bring AI risk into enterprise risk management, apply risk grading and approval for high-risk uses, keep human oversight at key points of high-risk applications and manage outsourcing and supply chain risk.

nodes.label: Microsoft reports replenishing more water than it withdrew in FY25
nodes.description: Blog on datacenter water intensity cites over $500 million in more than 75 water projects since 2020.

nodes.label: Council approves AI digital omnibus, delaying high-risk deadlines
nodes.description: Annex III high-risk duties move to December 2, 2027 and Annex I to August 2, 2028; adds explicit deepfake ban. This site has not confirmed the entry-into-force date.

nodes.label: Utah data center water reporting law takes effect
nodes.description: HB 76 requires large data centers drawing 75 acre feet or more a year to notify the state and file annual water use reports.

nodes.label: Big Tech AI proposal support falls to 7.6% average
nodes.description: AI proposals at Alphabet, Amazon and Meta averaged 7.6% in 2026, down from 9.8% in 2025 and 21.4% in 2024. The date shown is approximate.

nodes.label: About 135 companies excluded roughly 165 proposals in 2026
nodes.description: Post-season memo: about 45% of excluded proposals came from one individual filer; Glass Lewis found companies excluded fewer proposals than feared without staff relief.

nodes.label: SEC staff ends all Rule 14a-8 no-action responses
nodes.description: Staff stopped responding to all no-action requests, including (i)(1), and stopped sending will-not-object letters, "effective immediately, unless and until the Division announces otherwise." Companies are still required to submit Rule 14a-8(j) notices, and the statement says they should use the online Shareholder Proposal Form. Staff received no (i)(1) requests in the 2025-2026 season.

nodes.label: Ceres report 'Water Behind the Watts' on water used to power data centers
nodes.jurisdiction: US (VA, TX, CA, IL, GA, OH, AZ)
nodes.description: Finds data centers in seven states depend on about 3.4 trillion gallons of freshwater a year for their electricity; asks investors to seek fuller water disclosure from data center companies and power producers.

nodes.label: SEC sends 14a-8 rescission rule for interagency review
nodes.description: Ballotpedia reports the proposed rescission was submitted for interagency review and listed as economically significant on the regulatory agenda.

nodes.label: Shareholder proposal submissions fall nearly 25% in 2026
nodes.description: D.F. King reports 2026 shareholder proposal submissions were down nearly 25% from 2025, the lowest level in a decade.

nodes.label: Supreme People's Court issues opinions on AI dispute cases
nodes.description: 24 judicial rules for courts on AI cases, covering liability, use of public personal data in model training, AI product defects, open-source liability, deepfakes and algorithmic discrimination.

nodes.label: SEC proposes rescinding Rule 14a-8 and amending Rule 14a-4
nodes.description: Release 34-106383, File S7-2026-32 (September 16, 2026; 91 FR 59904), would end the federal shareholder proposal rule and amend Rule 14a-4, leaving proposals to state law and company governing documents. Comments were due November 20, 2026. It is a proposal, not a final rule.

nodes.label: CII calls rescission a solution in search of a problem
nodes.description: CII executive director Glenn Davis publicly opposed the proposal on release day, per a law firm summary. ICCR warned of losing an early warning system.

nodes.label: California requires data centers to report annual water use
nodes.description: AB 2619 ties water reporting to business licenses; AB 2469 requires water supply assessments for new data centers. Signing date per law firm.

nodes.label: Commission sets out EU sustainability rating scheme for data centers
nodes.description: A delegated regulation would give each EU data center above 500 kW a sustainability label based on reported energy and water use, waste heat reuse, clean energy and grid flexibility, with first labels expected in 2027. Parliament and Council had a two-month scrutiny period after September 21, 2026; entry into force is not confirmed.

nodes.label: NY State and NYC comptrollers oppose 14a-8 rescission
nodes.actor: NYS Comptroller DiNapoli; NYC Comptroller Levine
nodes.description: Joint statement opposed the proposal, urged companies to keep supporting shareholder proposals, and predicted lengthy legal challenges. A statement, not a docket letter.

nodes.label: Vanguard Investor Choice passes half a million participants
nodes.description: Pass-through voting participation grew more than sixfold; no single voting policy got over 38% of selections.

nodes.label: ISS STOXX: AI proposals grow while other E&S proposals fall
nodes.description: AI-related shareholder proposals at US companies grew over five years to 29 in 2026, while environmental and social proposals fell more than 60%. Average support for AI proposals fell to 10.3%.

nodes.label: China proposes adding AI technologies to its export control catalogue
nodes.actor: Ministry of Commerce; Ministry of Science and Technology
nodes.description: Proposes listing 23 AI technologies (large models, agents, computing clusters, information processing) as prohibited or restricted for export, excluding technology already public through open source or papers. Exporters must register such technology exports now, before the catalogue is finalized.

nodes.label: IIGCC research on bondholder stewardship of data center financing
nodes.description: Notes hyperscaler (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) bond issuance and sets out water and resilience questions bondholders can raise; mentions a forthcoming IIGCC data center playbook.

nodes.label: Rescission docket reaches 394 public comments
nodes.description: The docket for the proposal to rescind Rule 14a-8 showed 394 entries on November 25, 2026, the newest dated November 24; comments closed November 20. Letters on file include TIAA and Nuveen, L&G Asset Management, Wespath, the Washington State Investment Board, the Investment Adviser Association, the AJL Foundation with Oxfam America, the State Financial Officers Foundation and a staff memo of a meeting with CII. This site has not reviewed each letter's position.

nodes.label: Alphabet 2025: Enhanced Disclosure on Climate Goals
nodes.topic: Data center externalities
nodes.subtopic: Climate goals under rising AI data center energy use
nodes.proponent: Trillium ESG Global Equity Fund (lead) and co-filers
nodes.support_note: Not stated in the 8-K; this site computed it from the vote counts. The counts are votes cast under dual-class voting (Class B = 10 votes per share), so this site infers that support among holders without the 10-vote shares was higher than this figure.
nodes.plain_summary: Asks Alphabet to disclose additional information each year showing if and how it will meet its 2030 climate goals, given its growing greenhouse gas emissions.

policy_coverage.note: The EU AI Act makes general-purpose model providers document a model's known or estimated energy use for regulators on request; it requires no public data center emissions, energy or climate-goal reporting.
Voluntary: the 2023 Guidelines expect companies to set and report on emissions targets consistent with the Paris Agreement; they say nothing specific about data centers.
Texas makes loads of 75 MW or more pay interconnection study costs and disclose backup generation to the grid operator; it covers grid costs in ERCOT only, not emissions or investor reports.
Oregon puts users of 20 MW or more in their own rate class so data centers bear their grid costs; no emissions or public energy reporting.
Georgia Power may charge new customers above 100 MW their full transmission, distribution and generation costs; it is a utility rule in one state and requires no company disclosure.

EU data centers of 500 kW or more must report energy use, efficiency, renewable share and waste heat each year to an EU database; per-site data is not published and no company climate goals are required.
Companies in CSRD scope must report scope 1 to 3 emissions and energy use where material, which takes in data centers; it is not data center specific and Omnibus I narrowed who reports.
GB 40879 sets mandatory energy efficiency limits for new and expanded data centers in China; it does not require emissions or cost reporting.
The plan caps PUE for new large data centers in China at 1.25 (1.2 at hubs) through project energy review; it does not require company disclosure of energy, emissions or costs.
PUE, green electricity share and renewable energy plans become review criteria for new computing facilities in China; no public company reporting is required.

nodes.label: Alphabet 2025: Report on implementing AI app preload capabilities into Android OS (presented at the meeting; not in the proxy)
nodes.topic: Harms to people using AI products
nodes.subtopic: AI product strategy (floor proposal)
nodes.proponent: UNVERIFIED (the 8-K does not name the proponent)
nodes.support_note: Floor proposal: raised at the meeting, so shares voted earlier by proxy could not vote on it. Support is not comparable with proposals in the proxy; the 8-K gives the raw counts.
nodes.plain_summary: Asks for a report on building the ability to preload AI apps into the Android operating system.
nodes.plain_summary_note: Only the one-line description in the 8-K is public; no resolution text found.

nodes.label: Alphabet 2026: Enhanced Disclosure on Climate Goals
nodes.topic: Data center externalities
nodes.subtopic: Meeting GHG commitments given AI and data center energy demand
nodes.proponent: Trillium ESG Global Equity Fund (lead) and co-filers
nodes.support_note: Not stated in the 8-K; this site computed it from the vote counts. The counts are votes cast under dual-class voting (Class B = 10 votes per share), so this site infers that support among holders without the 10-vote shares was higher than this figure.
nodes.plain_summary: Asks Alphabet for a report explaining how it will meet its greenhouse gas commitments given rising energy demand from artificial intelligence and its planned data centers.

policy_coverage.note: The EU AI Act requires bias checks on high-risk systems' training data, now delayed to December 2027; it does not cover chatbot viewpoint bias or require a public report.

Colorado SB 26-189 requires notices, explanations and human review for automated decisions in jobs, lending, housing and other consequential areas from 2027, and drops the 2024 act's duty of reasonable care against algorithmic discrimination; it does not cover viewpoint bias or require public reports to investors.
The voluntary GPAI Code lists non-discrimination among risks signatory model providers should consider; it requires no public bias report.
NYC employers using automated hiring tools must publish annual independent bias audit summaries; the duty falls on employers in one city, not on AI vendors.
Illinois employers may not use AI with discriminatory effects in employment decisions from 2026; it covers one state and requires no public bias report.
TRAIGA bars AI developed or deployed with intent to unlawfully discriminate, but disparate impact alone is not enough; no bias testing or reporting.
Federal LLM contracts must require ideological neutrality and truth-seeking, which touches viewpoint bias; it applies only to models sold to federal agencies and requires no public report.
Korean high-impact AI operators must run risk management, give explanations and keep human oversight; there is no public bias report duty.

Providers must take effective measures to prevent discrimination by ethnicity, belief, country, region, sex, age, occupation or health in design and training data; no public bias audit or report is required.
Automated decisions using personal data must be transparent and fair with no unreasonable price discrimination; there is no reporting duty.
Recommendation services may not use algorithms for unreasonable price discrimination against consumers; broader bias review or reporting is not required.

The AI Safety Institute became the AI Security Institute.

Ofcom's investigation tests X against its Online Safety Act duties.

Sections 135 and 136 of the Act required the report and impact assessment.

The Act took effect after a one-year transition with its enforcement decree.
The government says feedback on the guardrails paper informed the National AI Plan and it will not proceed with mandatory guardrails at this time.

The labeling measures name the generative AI Interim Measures as a legal basis.

The CAC said TC260 drafted the framework to implement the Global AI Governance Initiative.
Framework 2.0 builds on the 2024 framework.
CAICT said the 2025 framework builds on the AIIA commitments of December 2024.
The agent opinions state they were made to implement the State Council AI Plus opinions.
The AI and energy action plan says it implements the AI Plus opinions.

The measures require AI companion providers to file under the Algorithmic Recommendation Provisions.
SAMR's 2025 finding came from the investigation it opened in December 2024.
The Supreme People's Court cited the Five-Year Plan's call for AI rules as background for its opinions.
